reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): Mandate check on all 8 legs (2026-07-29/30 data) found two positions have structurally broken the deep-value-dividend thesis: STLA no longer pays any dividend and has negative trailing earnings (Piper Sandler cut to Underweight, PT $4 vs spot $6.01) -- the opposite of a durable 6%+ yielder; GM has re-rated to a 45x trailing P/E with a 0.81% yield (was bought as a single-digit-P/E buyback story) -- no longer a value name, so I'm exiting both and banking the gains rather than holding a re-rated auto name for momentum reasons that don't fit this book's mandate. Among the survivors, VZ and MO are the best current fits (VZ: P/E 12.3, 5.99% yield, Q2 beat, buyback raised to $4.5B, multiple analyst upgrades; MO: P/E 15.7, 5.66% yield, EPS +7.3%, price-target hikes) so I'm adding to both. I trimmed BTI slightly (5,500-seat job cuts, fresh class-action exposure, one analyst flagging dividend-sustainability questions), trimmed PFE slightly (P/E has drifted to ~19x, above the low-teens target, though the 6.84% yield and recent FDA/EU approvals keep it a core holding), and trimmed C modestly after today's -4% post-earnings drop on second-half expense guidance (still cheap at 13.8x and near tangible book, so kept as a real position, not exited). KHC held unchanged -- still trades below book with a 5.86% yield despite packaged-food headwinds. The freed capital from the two exits is not fully redeployed into unresearched names; a larger cash buffer (23%, earning 4% APY) is the honest reflection of reduced conviction after cutting two legs, not forced diversification.
research_notes: Checked live quotes/news (stockanalysis.com, as of 2026-07-29 close) for all 8 book positions plus Ford as a potential auto replacement. Key findings: STLA pays no dividend and has negative trailing earnings (Piper Sandler cut to Underweight, $4 PT vs $6.01 spot) -- thesis broken, exited. GM has re-rated to a 45x trailing P/E with only a 0.81% yield despite a Q2 beat and raised guidance -- no longer a value/dividend name, exited. VZ and MO both screen as cheap, high-yield, and have positive fresh news (VZ: Google fiber deal, raised buyback, analyst upgrades; MO: EPS growth, PT hikes) -- added to both. BTI has fresh legal/restructuring risk (9,000 job cuts, class-action ruling) and one dividend-sustainability flag -- trimmed. PFE's P/E has drifted to ~19x (above mandate range) despite a strong 6.84% yield and positive regulatory news -- trimmed. C dropped 4% on 2H expense guidance despite an EPS beat -- trimmed modestly, kept as still-cheap core position. KHC unchanged, still fits (below book, 5.86% yield). Checked Ford (F) as a potential replacement auto name but its trailing P/E is n/a (negative GAAP earnings) and yield is only 3.93%, so it doesn't clear the mandate's bar; freed capital was left in cash (23%) rather than forced into a new name.
